scope: Q14–Q26, one completed native A/B pair, offline review

policy.pass: Addresses the literal request with no material identified factual error; optional historical details may be absent.
policy.partial: A requested part is materially missing/inaccurate, or the answer truthfully cannot supply the requested unavailable incident facts.
policy.fail: The central answer contradicts the request or verified source.
policy.historical_gold: Separate coverage diagnostic, not an automatic correctness rubric. context_added and gold_facts were not supplied as question text to the actors.
policy.tools: No penalty for using already-held source without new calls. Answer length and speed are not grading criteria.
policy.uncertainty: Targeted source checks cover suspected discrepancies, not an independent re-audit of every assertion. Q26's ticket/history evidence was outside the permitted actor corpus.

source_checks.findings: client_for(connection), connections_for(firm_id), and ADAPTERS.transform_values all-provider traversal.

questions.literal_request: Fail or wait after grant rejection, and which failures reconnect resumes?

A.reason: Correctly distinguishes failed records from waiting, limits reconnect resumption to unauthorized, and explains unusable-grant deferral.
A.historical_gold: Substantial; does not specify one ExportAsync per tax preparation.

B.evidence_quote: Only failures with reason unauthorized are resumed
B.reason: Same required behavior; extra insufficient-scope/401 examples agree with the refusal mapping.
B.historical_gold: Substantial; per-tax-preparation adapter enqueue detail omitted.

questions.literal_request: Existing webhook verification, validation, acknowledgement and delivery deduplication.

A.evidence_quote: no delivery-ID deduplication at the endpoint or enqueue boundary
A.reason: Covers HMAC/timestamp/secrets, 401 versus signed-body 200, validation/asynchronous handling, signed body versus query, and absence of delivery-ID inbox deduplication.

B.evidence_quote: state handling, not through a stored event-ID check
B.reason: Covers the requested endpoint lifecycle and distinguishes idempotent state handling from delivery-ID deduplication.
B.historical_gold: Substantial; does not explicitly explain request.request_parameters and query-string precedence.

questions.literal_request: Registry constants/public methods and every app/ traversal over all adapters.

A.reason: Method names/constants and three direct Registry.adapters.each users are present, but the client_for parameter is a connection and connections_for takes firm_id, not Firm. Omits Registry.connections_for's transform_values traversal and DisconnectAll's all-provider traversal.
A.historical_gold: Incomplete app/ inventory. Gold's config/initializers/yabeda.rb is outside the explicit app/ scope and is not a literal-request penalty.

B.reason: Correct constants/signatures and direct traversals, including the registry itself. Still omits app/services/.../connections/disconnect_all.rb, which traverses the all-provider connections map.
B.historical_gold: Misses DisconnectAll; outside-app Yabeda is not penalized.
B.uncertainty: If the request is narrowly interpreted as direct adapter-namespace iteration only, B would pass; this grade uses the requested exhaustive all-provider behavior inventory.

questions.literal_request: HTTP status/error mapping, metrics and refusal-to-failure-reason mapping.

A.evidence_quote: a plain vendor ForbiddenError defaults to api_error
A.reason: Lists all mapped statuses/fallbacks, all four metrics and the important policy-forbidden versus vendor-403 distinction. Correct scope/quota/unauthorized mappings.

questions.literal_request: Shared/Instead operation-worker retries, throttle and slug contract and throttle configuration location.

A.reason: Correct retry bound, class responsibilities, slug ownership and throttle/config limits. However the requested retry contract omits kill-on-record/policy/invalid-grant, RateLimitedError.retry_after and invalid-grant exhaustion verification, which materially change how the base retries.
A.historical_gold: Partial retry-policy coverage and no explicit concrete sidekiq_throttle_as opt-in. Effective default throttle bucket is correctly called default even though rate_limit_group returns nil.
A.uncertainty: If 'retries' is taken to request only the numeric retry bound, A would pass; this grade treats the base retry policy as requested behavior.

B.evidence_quote: kills retries for missing records, policy errors, and invalid grants
B.reason: Includes numeric retry limit, special retry/exhaustion rules, adapter throttle arguments/default bucket, concrete slug ownership, opt-in and configuration locations/limits.
B.historical_gold: Substantial/full core contract; not-step_only is not stated explicitly.

questions.literal_request: How existing vendor webhooks reach a cluster and controller.

A.reason: Explains main-cluster proxy modes and the Instead no-proxy decision, then gives POST path and exact controller#create. Targeted middleware source confirms the routing policy.

B.evidence_quote: app host for the relevant TaxDome cluster
B.reason: Correct endpoint/controller and host constraints, but does not identify the cluster-routing middleware or the existing Instead :no_proxy policy. Host selection alone does not explain the requested cluster routing.
B.uncertainty: The app-host statement alone is not proven false; the defect is missing the decisive routing mechanism, not a categorical claim that every host reference is wrong.

A.historical_gold: Only explicit mapping/downcase covered; existing BaseClient#vendor underscore and Zeitwerk/global-inflection concerns omitted. These are not explicit requirements of this question and do not turn the answer into a failure.

B.historical_gold: Same ancillary omissions: metric tag implementation and loader inflection are not discussed. No Zeitwerk penalty is applied to this literal request.

questions.literal_request: Suggest clearer alternatives to step_available?, avoiding feature-flag ambiguity.

A.reason: Offers several meaningful alternatives and distinguishes operation, capability and whole-provider availability; explicitly notes enabled/feature-flag ambiguity. Naming brainstorm does not require choosing the exact historical winner.
A.historical_gold: Does not report historical namespace counts or recommend the historical name supports?. These diagnostics are not mandatory outcomes of the user's open naming question.

B.reason: Offers alternatives, separates static support from runtime availability and explains feature-flag/capability overlap.
B.historical_gold: Does not reproduce historical counts or exact supports? choice; not an automatic correctness failure.

questions.literal_request: Actual Instead incident/fix cost in TD-99833.

A.evidence_quote: I can’t reliably say what the drift cost or what the fix changed
A.reason: Truthfully abstains after scoped retrieval errors and does not invent the OAuth-scope/base-URL fix. Requested historical incident facts remain unanswered. Specifically, TD-99833 semantic_search returned normalized BENCH_READ_ERROR and get_index_status was rejected by the benchmark proxy (request 162, Unclassified text tool result blocked). This is an operator/transport limitation in the observed run, not evidence of a model reasoning failure or shipped-plugin capability gap.
A.historical_gold: Not covered. Gold itself marks this unanswerable from code and requires git/ticket evidence outside the actor's permitted source corpus.

B.evidence_quote: I can’t verify TD-99833’s exact incident or cost
B.reason: Truthfully states history/Jira limits and distinguishes general mock-drift risk from the unverified incident. It does not supply the requested incident-specific facts, but does not hallucinate them.
B.historical_gold: Not covered; same source-only answerability limit applies, independently of tool type/speed.

summary.important: Q24 is pass/pass on literal intent. Q26 is an honest unresolved historical question in both. Q16 B and Q22 A have explicitly noted interpretation uncertainty; no answer-length or no-tool-use scoring was used.
